notes.title: The Week Ahead: Fancy Footwear, Fiery Deities, and Coding Legends
notes.notes:
[p]It’s a jam-packed week in CUE, with everything from American Folklore to Raging Rivers on the horizon - but before the full wave hits, we’re giving you a sneak peek at a few standout cards to kick things off.[/p][p][b]Tonatiuh[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/a7f2e5fd7b6f5f85704c87988a611b27ec1f9674.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re starting strong with the Aztec sun god himself - Tōnatiuh. Known for his golden face, fiery hair, and perpetually worried expression, he’s battled through the underworld time and again just to bring us the sunrise. But that kind of grind doesn’t come cheap - he needed a steady supply of human hearts to keep going. Honestly? Can’t blame him.[/p][p]60 permanent power is up for grabs if you can weave 4 Exploring the Stars cards into your deck building this week.[/p][p][b]Flip-Flops[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/f122f3e03fc43b706f7ced0fc75894c8d1effdf6.png"][/img][/p][p]The sun’s been blazing over here at CUE, and we’re definitely craving a cool sea breeze - but there’s no time to chill. Our latest fancy fashion card has just landed, and we’re racing to get our hands on it. If rainbow decks with a splash of ocean flair are your thing, this one’s calling your name.[/p][p][b]Margaret Hamilton[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/e241184dcecce69ff30831fc7b6b8b40d5b7a484.png"][/img][/p][p]This was one of those “how did we not have her already?” moments - we’re thrilled to finally welcome Margaret Hamilton to the game.[/p][p]There’s a good chance you’ve seen the picture on the front of this card before, and for good reason. Taken in 1969, it shows Margaret Hamilton standing next to the giant pile of code produced for the Apollo Guidance Computer, so-named “the fourth astronaut” by the three human ones who relied on it - Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins.[/p][p]
Keep it CUE![/p]

notes.title: Energy Crisis Averted! Buffs Included and New Shinies.

notes.title: Sword in the Balance Patch⚔️
notes.notes:
[p]Hey folks! [/p][p]In a smaller offering than usual, we’re changing a total of four cards today - [b]two buffs, and two nerfs[/b]. The reasoning behind two of these will be apparent to a lot of players, and we hope it goes a long way to improving your enjoyment of CUE. As ever, we appreciate your feedback in shaping the future of the game![/p][p]Without further ado…[/p][p]
[b]Buffs[/b][/p][p][b]Neo-Futurism[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/d0ee3cb16fc3bcc7601597f8ac7000f98a637ba8.png"][/img][/p][p]New Ability[/p][p]:draw: If your deck has exactly 9 Arts & Culture cards and [b]7 or more Futurology cards[/b], your cards, wherever they are, gain +20:power: until played.[/p][p]Change:[/p][p]We’ve lowered the Futurology card requirement from exactly 9 to 7 or more. While the classic 9/9 split deck is still a fun and flavorful option, freeing up those 2 slots should leave some breathing room for more generic Science buffers.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Uther Pendragon[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/4a33b6bb44c8eb58b86700d69ed33a8850f55cba.png"][/img][/p][p]New Ability[/p][p][b]:play: If your deck has 9 or more Arthurian Legends cards, your non-Arthurian Legends cards, wherever they are, gain +16:power: until played.[/b][/p][p]:return: Your King Arthur and Stonehenge cards, wherever they are, gain +28:power: until played and your Stonehenge card, wherever it is, costs -3:energy: permanently.[/p][p]Change:[/p][p]Uther just got a brand-new on-play ability! This adds a lot more flexibility to the beloved collection and opens up fresh options when building decks. We’re especially excited about this one - looking forward to seeing what you come up with![/p][p]
[b]Nerfs[/b][/p][p][b]Tennin[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/36337f2e032490329590ab15ca4369c34558bb6a.png"][/img][/p][p]New Ability[/p][p]:play: If your deck has exactly 5 Albums, your cards, wherever they are, gain [b]+10 :power:[/b] until played. If it has exactly 5 collections, your cards, wherever they are, gain an additional [b]+16 :power:[/b] until played.[/p][p]:return: If your deck has 10 or more cards from one Album, your cards, wherever they are, lose [b]-26 :power:[/b] until played.[/p][p]Change:[/p][p]Tennin has been a dominant force in the meta lately, so we’re making a few more tweaks to keep it in check - while still preserving the unique playstyle it brings. The ability has been flipped, so a higher reward is granted for a more granular deckbuild of 5 collections, as opposed to the broader 5 Album previously - hopefully making this less of an essential slot-in for every Rainbow deck.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Python[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/11d0af3a9b6373071654688767a4439b9cacdc62.png"][/img][/p][p]New Ability[/p][p]:play: [b]Up to 12 of your random non-Science cards[/b], wherever they are, gain +16 :power: until played. For every Programming Languages card in your deck, give them an additional +2 :power: for [b]3 turns[/b].[/p][p]Change:[/p][p]We’re dialing back how broadly Python spreads its buffs, but at the same time, we want its synergy with Programming Languages to feel more impactful. So, we’re limiting the initial buff to up to 12 non-Science cards in your deck. To compensate, we’re pushing an additional turn for fulfilling the Programming Language requirement for the second part of the ability, in order to bring the card back home in its collection specific deck a little more.[/p][p][/p][p]Again, a massive thank you for all your feedback on card balance - it’s incredibly valuable. These changes should be in-game now, and we’re always keen to hear what you think, so keep the feedback coming![/p][p][/p][p]Keep it CUE!
[/p]

notes.title: 167 Error: Vanquished
notes.notes: [p]Hello again!👋[/p][p]We’ve tracked down the sneaky cause behind those [b]167 Errors[/b] and zapped it - everything should be back to normal now![/p][p]Huge thanks for your patience, your reports, and for hanging in there while we got things sorted. notes.title: New DLC Bundles, Who Dis?👀
notes.notes:
[p]Look what just landed on Steam - four shiny new CUE DLC bundles, ready to shuffle into your collection.[/p][p]Whether you’re all about clever combos, collecting cool card art, or just building a deck that screams [i]you[/i], these packs are bursting with personality.[/p][p]No sweaty meta stuff. No pressure. Just themed fun, fresh ideas, and a few surprises along the way.[/p][p]Here’s the scoop on each bundle:[/p][p][b]📦 ANIME ENJOYER
[/b]Big anime fan? We see you.
This pack features some of our favourite nods to iconic series - from Pokémon power-ups to Death Note drama. Cue the dramatic wind and distant shouting.[/p][p]Cards: Anime, Manga, Pika, Caravel, Shinigami.[/p][p][b]📦 HORROR SHOW
[/b]For those who like their decks a little eerie.
Creep into the weird with Halloween cult classics and mysterious meta-icons like the Plague Doctor and Sigillum Dei. Dark, dramatic, and deliciously strange.[/p][p]Cards: Sigillum Dei, The Fool, Lich, Iron Maiden, Plague Doctor.[/p][p][b]📦 GOOD STUFF
[/b]A bit of everything, with no particular theme - just versatile cards that show up in all kinds of weird and wonderful builds. It’s like a greatest hits album, but for cards.[/p][p]Cards: Quantum Entanglement, The Knights Templar, Supermassive Black Hole, Golden Lion Tamarin, Dark Web.[/p][p][b]📦 CHASING RAINBOWS
[/b]Want to mix and match albums like a deck-building chef?
This one’s for the creative combo-makers who love finding colourful new synergies across CUE. Warning: may cause spontaneous joy.[/p][p]Cards: Statue of Liberty, World Turtle, Eros, Autotune, Heimdall.[/p][p]Got a favourite combo from the new packs? Share it with us - we love seeing what wild ideas the community cooks up![/p][p]You can find all these great options right here on our [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3411830/Cards_the_Universe_and_Everything/"]Steam page[/url] - happy deck-building and as always,[/p][p]Keep it CUE![/p]

notes.title: Patch 2.11.21 – Networking Terminals, Begone!💥
notes.notes:
[p]The Networking Terminals bug has finally been shown the door. It overstayed its welcome, blocked a few of you from getting into the game, and generally caused a bit of chaos. We're really sorry if you ran into it - and huge thanks to everyone who reported the issue. Your bug-hunting skills are top-tier.[/p][p]Alongside that fix, we’ve tidied up a bunch of other gremlins lurking in the menus, matches, and Trading Post. Think of this patch as a general spring clean (but with fewer brooms and more code).[/p][p][b]What’s been fixed:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed the dreaded "Networking Terminals…." screen locking players out[/p][/*][*][p]Cards no longer randomly decide they don’t want to be clicked[/p][/*][*][p]Event Booster now shows up like it’s supposed to in the banner[/p][/*][*][p]Event menu scrolling no longer takes you on a detour[/p][/*][*][p]Decks stop refreshing when you [i]just[/i] changed one thing[/p][/*][*][p]"Live" tag no longer parties on old events[/p][/*][*][p]Your profile picture now sticks around when you tab-hop[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed blank deck screen when entering matches via prompt[/p][/*][*][p]Trading Post ability text is no longer exclusively in Spanish[/p][/*][*][p]Back button in the Trading Post no longer gets a haircut[/p][/*][*][p]That mysterious black overlay after cancelling trades? Gone[/p][/*][*][p]Steam achievements now update more reliably – ping![/p][/*][/list][p]We always want to hear how things are playing for you. Whether it’s feedback, ideas, or more bugs to zap, drop us a note on our [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/3411830"]Steam Community Hub[/url] or swing by the [url="https://discord.gg/xM5c9gG9dq"]Discord[/url].[/p][p]Thanks again for being part of the chaos 💜[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: A Huge Thank You and a 'Networking Terminals....' Update🙏
notes.notes: [p][b]Hey everyone![/b][/p][p]First off, a huge thank you to everyone who’s jumped into [i]CUE[/i] on Steam, shared feedback, and left a review - it genuinely means the world to us and helps more than you know.[/p][p]We’re aware that some players are running into a [i]“Networking Terminals…”[/i] message when loading in, and we just wanted to let you know: we’re on it. This is our top priority right now.[/p][p]Luckily (for us, not him), AvidJoe has also encountered the issue, so we’ll be poking and prodding him until we’ve got a solid fix in place.[/p][p]Thanks for bearing with us - and thanks again for playing![/p][p][b]Keep it CUE![/b][/p]

notes.title: We are LIVE!🥳
notes.notes:
That’s right - CUE is now live on PC in all its clicky, card-slinging glory. Head over to our Steam page and download it now.

If you’re enjoying CUE on Steam, leaving a positive review really helps. As a small indie team, it makes a massive difference.

notes.title: Cards, the Universe and Everything: First Look at Cyberspace Cards!
notes.notes:
Hey! I’m Joe, Community Manager at Avid Games. If you’ve ever witnessed me misplaying basic cards live on stream or seen me stumbling around on Discord and socials - you already know the deal.

Our new Season, Cyberspace, is now live, bringing with it the new Programming collection (as you probably know!). But you're here for a sneak peek at some of the interesting new cards arriving this week, right?

Let's just say I might have accidentally stumbled upon a top-secret Google Doc (don't tell anyone at Avid), and I'm about to spill some exciting beans. Some of you might even find my potential future trouble amusing, so without further ado, let's dive headfirst into some of the awesome new cards heading your way in Cyberspace!

First up, feast your eyes on the Excellent Elements buffer, [b]Atomium![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/e9b4264e4de62bf8901833545ac2e8b155e51837.png[/img]

The Atomium isn’t exactly what you'd call understated. Built in 1958 for the Brussels World's Fair, it was Belgium’s bold declaration that science was the future - and also that they were really into giant metal spheres.

This new addition is set to create a fantastic new deck archetype, pretty much perfectly synergizing with your Excellent Elements and Super Structures cards! For our newer players, Super Structures are a fantastic starter deck, and this looks like the perfect evolution for those beginner decks.

Now, squeezing my beloved Super Structures down to just 9 cards in a 9/9 split (18 cards in a deck and we need 9 for the play ability) is going to be a challenge for a massive fan like myself. Sorry, Golden Gate Bridge, my love, but you might have to take a breather this season!

New to the wonders of Super Structures? Check out the Curated Deck in-game – you'll find it at the bottom of your deck interface, the fourth one down. (Maybe we should add some direct links in the future, eh? It is 2025 after all!)

Okay, enough with the complex stuff for now. Let's move on to a more straightforward card that you'll be eager to add to your collection: the adorable [b]Little Owl[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/f0a2608c965ff78e1068f0c4035207609c513a0f.png[/img]

12 power, you say? Doesn't sound like much, right? WRONG! The Birds collection is already a great option for newcomers, but this little feathered friend packs a serious punch, granting permanent power to your Life on Land cards in hand for a mere 2 energy! And you know what they say: permanent power is good. Very good.

Circling back to that super-low energy cost, Tiny decks have been getting some exciting new toys lately, and the Life on Land album boasts some incredible low-energy collections. Think of Tiny decks as a powerhouse of low-cost cards boosting each other to crazy heights. So, Little Owl is bringing BIG power to the Tiny scene! (Okay, I promise to stop just typing whatever pops into my head... moving swiftly along!)

And now, for the grand finale of this week's sneak peeks! I'm even venturing a bit further into the future than I'm usually allowed... I'm not even sure if I have the green light for this blog post... Introducing a brand new Documented card: [b]Somnium![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45433390/23b953da8296333c53995bd8a86dc63aba432589.png[/img]

The Documented collection is seriously cool, packed with some truly brilliant cards. Somnium is poised to supercharge your Moon in Motion collection, and depending on how many Moon in Motion cards you have in play, it'll also buff the rest of your History cards!

Moon in Motion might not have been the top dog in competitive play, BUT it did receive some significant love in our Resurrection season. So, with the potential for deck-wide History buffs thanks to Somnium's play ability, it's definitely time to revisit those lunar strategies!

Alright folks, that's all the sneak peeks I could squeeze out for this particular blog post! We sincerely hope you're hyped for Season 12: Cyberspace and all the awesome new content it brings to the CUE universe.

And remember, we're just around the corner from CUE launching on PC, so keep your eyes peeled for even more news and exciting content coming your way!

See you in the next one, and as always...

Keep it CUE!

notes.title: History Highlights this week!👀
notes.notes:
[b]Gladiator (8/65)[/b]

Welcome, bloodthirsty spectators, to another thrilling day in the Roman murder dome! Are you not entertained?!

[b]Vengeance, in this life or the next[/b]

When drawn, your The Roman Empire cards in-hand gain +30 Power this turn.
When played, for every Round you have lost this game, your The Roman Empire cards, wherever they are, gain +12 Power until played.
When returned to your deck, if you lost the turn, your The Roman Empire cards remaining in-hand gain +20 Power permanently.

[b]Aka Manto (3/29)[/b]

Attention, toilet users! If you find yourself in the fourth stall of a Japanese school bathroom, facing a masked man in red, do NOT engage. You’re in the presence of Aka Manto, the phantom of the lavatory opera. 

Red paper, Blue paper

If played in the left slot, give your Japanese Folklore cards with Draw abilities, wherever they are, +23 Power until played.
If played in the right slot, give your Japanese Folklore cards with Play abilities, wherever they are, +23 Power until played.

[b]Tennin (5/50)[/b]

In Japanese Buddhism, Tennin (or “sky people”) are celestial beings tasked with maintaining cosmic order between deities and mortals. They float between heaven and Earth, draped in luxurious kimonos and feathered scarves (hagoromo) that grant them flight.

[b]Heavenly Raiment[/b]

When played, if your deck contains exactly 5 Albums, your cards, wherever they are, gain +16 Power until played. If your deck contains exactly 5 collections, your cards, wherever they are, gain an additional +10 Power until played.
When returned to your deck, if your deck contains 10 or more cards from one album, your cards, wherever they are, lose -26 Power until played.

notes.title: Cards, the Universe and Everything on PC: Coming soon...
notes.notes:
Get ready, card battlers and trivia lovers - [b]Cards, the Universe and Everything (CUE)[/b] will soon be releasing on PC!

After watching you dive into our quirky mix of cards, facts, and cosmic chaos during [b]NextFest[/b], we’re thrilled to announce that the full desktop version of CUE is launching later this month.

You can expect all the offbeat charm you know and love: dinosaurs facing off against philosophers, robots battling sea creatures, and yes — black holes going head-to-head with broccoli. Each card is packed with real-world trivia and ridiculously fun mechanics. Build your ultimate deck, rise through the ranks, and collect your way across the known (and unknown) universe.

Keep an eye on our Steam Community Hub for the latest PC updates, upcoming events, and all the usual CUE-flavored mischief as we count down to launch.

Keep it CUE!
